column5: item

column3: Is the code freely available?
column5: Method's code is freely available
The code can be run on a freely available platform（python、R...）

column3: Is the code version controlled?
column5: The code is available on a public version controlled repository, such as Github

column3: Is the code contained into an easy to install package? Is it discoverable?
column5: The code is provided as a "package", exposing functionality through functions or shell commands
The code can be easily installed through a repository such as CRAN, Bioconductor, PyPI, CPAN, debian packages, ...

column3: Are dependencies clearly stated and available?
column5: Dependencies are clearly stated in the tutorial or in the code
Dependencies are automatically installed（or requirements.txt,pyproject.toml,setup.py...）

column3: Does the tool have a graphical user interface?
column5: The tool can be run using a graphical user interface, either locally or on a web server
The tool can be run through the command line or through a programming language

column3: Do the functions and objects have a consistent naming?
column5: Functions/commands have well chosen names
Arguments/parameters have well chosen names

column3: Do the functions have a consistent style?
column5: Code has a consistent style
Code follows (basic) good practices in the programming language of choice, for example PEP8 or the tidyverse style guide

column3: Is code frequently duplicated?
column5: Duplicated code is minimal

column3: Does the code expose certain steps in the method as self-contained functions or commands?
column5: The method is exposed to the user as self-contained functions or commands

column3: Does the package allow plotting of (intermediate) results?
column5: Plotting functions are provided for the final and/or intermediate results

column3: Does the package include dummy proofing?
column5: Package contains dummy proofing, i.e. testing whether the parameters and data supplied by the user make sense and are useful

column3: Does the package include a system to ask for support?
column5: There is a support ticket system, for example on Github
The authors respond to tickets and issues are resolved within a reasonable time frame

column3: Does the repository follow a development model, such as GitFlow?
column5: The repository separates the development code from master code, for example using git master en developer branches
The repository has created releases, or several branches corresponding to major releases.
The repository has branches for the development of separate features.

column3: Is there a tutorial available for the method? Does this tutorial show everything the user needs?
column5: A tutorial or vignette is available
The tutorial has example results
The tutorial has real example data
The tutorial showcases the method on several datasets (1=0, 2=0.5, >2=1)

column3: Is the purpose and usage of each function documented?
column5: The purpose and usage of functions/commands is documented
The parameters of functions/commands are documented
The output of functions/commands is documented

column3: Is the code documented inline?
column5: Inline documentation is present in the code

column3: Are all important parameters available to the user?
column5: All important parameters are exposed to the user

column3: Is unexpected output generated by the method?
column5: No unexpected output messages are generated by the method
No unexpected files, folders or plots are generated
No unexpected warnings during runtime or compilation are generated

column3: Was postprocessing necessary to get the output of the method into a useful format?
column5: The postprocessing necessary to extract the relevant output from the method is minimal (1), moderate (0.5) or extensive (0)

column3: Is the method published?
column5: The method is published

column3: Is the method published in a peer-reviewed journal?
column5: The paper is published in a peer-reviewed journal

column3: Is the methods usefulness shown in the paper?
column5: The paper shows the method's usefulness on several (1), one (0.25) or no real datasets.
The paper quantifies the accuracy of the method

column3: Does the paper assess method robustness?
column5: The paper assessed method robustness (to eg. noise, subsampling, parameter changes, stability)

column3: Did the code need significant adjustment to run
column5: Able to run analysis pipeline with minimal/no changes to code
column6: Able to run analysis pipeline with minimal/no changes to code (1) or required significant changes (0)

column3: Does the method require domain expertise to run?
column5: Experience in deep learning/Python/R is required (0), or not required (1)

column3: Are extra user actions required for application?
column5: Able to handle input/output data formats with no additional code required.
column6: (By default, both input and output formats are assumed to be AnnData, where the output AnnData contains new coordinates.)（1）Not needed at all (fully automated).（0.5） Minor adjustments needed (e.g., only reading/outputting coordinates).（0）Requires additional custom code (e.g., only returning matched points).

column5: The user is not required to provide any extra information (e.g., region labels).
